headline: 14 contracts catalogued across Ethereum and Sonic chains; 6 Ethereum-side gateway contracts (3 proxies + 3 implementations active) and 8 Sonic-side contracts; multisig admin roles confirmed by audit but multisig addresses not yet on-chain-verified this run.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced TokenDeposit (0xa1E2481a9CD0Cb0447EeB1cbc26F1b3fff3bec20) with tag 'Sonic Labs: Sonic Gateway', confirmed as ERC1967 proxy with $64M TVL and 65,289 transactions as of 2026-10-06. Current implementation is 0xAdE2eF0101278fe11490F2EE2aaD7915a094ADe9 (upgraded 2025-04-17), superseding the docs-listed 0x4cbd824685F1E21B119F230B54d65C5a7D2a5330.

Official deployed-contracts doc at docs.soniclabs.com/sonic/build-on-sonic/contract-addresses lists 6 Ethereum-side contracts (MPTProofVerifier, StateOracle, ValidatorsRegistry, TokenPairs proxy+impl, TokenDeposit proxy+impl, DirectExitAdministrator, UpdateManager proxy+impl) and 8 Sonic-side contracts. All addresses recorded in admin_addresses[].

OpenZeppelin audit (blog.openzeppelin.com/sonic-gateway-audit, commit 558465d, timeline 2024-09-24 to 2024-10-21) lists in-scope contracts: Bridge, TokenDeposit, TokenPairs, StateOracle, ValidatorsRegistry, UpdateManager, DirectExitAdministrator, ExitAdministrator, MPTProofVerifier, MessageBus, ActivityMonitor, SFCUpdateVerifier, MintedERC20. Confirms multisig admin roles on Bridge, ExitAdministrator, TokenDeposit, TokenPairs, UpdateManager. Quantstamp certificate URL surfaced (certificate.quantstamp.com/full/sonic-gateway/fbb78575-...) but not fetched. Certora audit referenced but URL not discovered this run.

GitHub repo Fantom-foundation/Bridge identified from OZ audit at commit 558465d3aba2ffae1a4436a2fc14c723b82926df. Direct fetch of github.com/Fantom-foundation/Bridge failed (site returned access error). Deployment artifacts not walked this run; repo URL recorded.

Protocol.chains lists only 'Ethereum'; Sonic chain contracts documented in D2 but Sonic is the counterpart chain, not a protocol.chains entry. All Sonic-side addresses recorded separately. No additional chains (BSC, Polygon, Arbitrum, etc.) found to have Sonic Gateway deployments.

No factory contract identified in the Ethereum-side Gateway contracts. TokenPairs maintains a registry of supported token pairs; no child-enumeration read performed this run as no surfacer URL was pre-built. Recorded in unknowns[].

Role taxonomy applied: TokenDeposit = vault (proxy); StateOracle = oracle; ValidatorsRegistry = other; TokenPairs = other (proxy); UpdateManager = admin (proxy); DirectExitAdministrator = guardian; MPTProofVerifier = other. Multisig admin addresses not discovered as concrete on-chain addresses this run.

All addresses in admin_addresses[] traced to fetched docs page (docs.soniclabs.com/sonic/build-on-sonic/contract-addresses) and/or Etherscan fetch. Multisig controller addresses behind UpdateManager and other contracts are not yet enumerated — no concrete 0x addresses surfaced from fetched sources for the multisigs themselves.

protocol_metadata.about: Sonic Gateway is a canonical bridge between Ethereum and the Sonic layer-1 blockchain, enabling users to deposit ERC-20 tokens (USDC, WETH, EURC, FTM, and others) into a TokenDeposit contract on Ethereum, which are then claimable as minted IOU tokens on Sonic via Merkle proof. Withdrawals from Sonic burn IOU tokens and unlock the originals on Ethereum through the same Merkle proof mechanism. An off-chain IBC relay network of Sonic validators updates StateOracle contracts on both chains with verified Merkle roots; a 14-day dead-bridge fallback via DirectExitAdministrator allows users to recover locked Ethereum-side funds if the bridge is inactive. Administrative roles across all contracts are held by multisig wallets, with the UpdateManager serving as the central upgrade controller on both chains.
